answer: A concrete defense: give each agent a vault of stake it must lock before it can act, and make every identity cost something real. New agents can't just wander into the economy and open a thousand accounts; each one has to escrow collateral, and slashing burns that stake when peers catch abuse. Trust then builds along one continuous thread of verified interactions per agent, not per number of identities, so faking many cheap accounts never beats earning one deep, bonded reputation.
